page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-176 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8481C processors. The system provides 176 virtual CPUs across 88 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, supported by 105 MB of shared L3 cache and dedicated per-core L1 and L2 caches. It is configured with 352 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. The underlying hardware incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), targeting vectorized and matrix arithmetic operations. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel compute throughput, placing the multi-core stress-ng performance and overall PassMark CPU score within the top tier. Extended instruction and cryptographic execution tests also achieve top-tier rankings, enabled by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 458.9 GB/sec, supporting fast throughput for high-concurrency tasks. Consequently, the instance delivers top-tier performance in static web serving throughput at 126.23 GB/sec and Redis SET operations exceeding 164 million operations per second.

Single-threaded performance scores across Geekbench and stress-ng fall within the median range, indicating that raw execution gains depend primarily on thread parallelism rather than isolated single-core frequency. Compute-dense jobs like image processing, ray tracing, and Clang compilation show strong execution times due to the high core count. In qualitative cost-efficiency terms, the high-density compute allocation maximizes throughput per instance for parallel workloads, though workloads requiring disproportionately large memory footprints or high local disk IOPS may face architectural tradeoffs.

The c3-highcpu-176 instance is suitable for massively multi-threaded compute workloads, including high-concurrency static web serving, software build pipelines, distributed cache infrastructure, and CPU-based matrix inference operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-176 is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 176 dedicated vCPUs across 88 physical cores with a 2.7 GHz base clock speed and 352 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached volumes. Benefiting from hardware accelerators such as Intel AMX and AVX-512, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute in stress-ng and PassMark benchmarks, alongside high-throughput uncached memory access. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput both test in the top decile. While single-threaded performance remains within the middle range, the extensive core count delivers strong outcomes in distributed compilation and image processing. This instance is best matched for large-scale parallel processing, distributed caching, web serving fleets, and CPU-driven inference tasks.
